---
title: "Roadmap and open questions"
description: "What is still undecided or unproven — and where feedback helps most."
---

These workflows are in active use but still settling. This page lists what
is already known to be open, so you don't have to ask — and where your
experience would help decide.

## How to give feedback {#feedback}

For now, open an [issue](https://github.com/FlorianSchw/package-workflows/issues):
a missing input, a behaviour that doesn't fit your package, an idea, or a
point from the list below.

::: {.callout-note}
## Please no pull requests for now
The repository has no branch model or review rules yet, so pull requests
can't be handled properly. Please open an issue instead — pull requests
may be closed without review until this is set up.
:::

## Open questions

### Versioning

All workflows are referenced at `@main`, so every change reaches every
caller on its next run. Versioned releases (`@v1`, with breaking changes
in `@v2`) will follow once the inputs have settled.

*Feedback wanted:* inputs you miss, or ones you never need.

### Suggestion thresholds

Bot suggestions are only proposed for [certain reasons](suggestions.qmd#what-gets-proposed):
documentation that is missing, inaccurate or incomplete, and tests that
cover a new code path, an error, an edge case or a likely regression.
These lists are a first setting.

*Feedback wanted:* suggestion PRs that weren't worth it, or improvements
you expected but didn't get.

### Model per task

All suggestion workflows currently use the same Claude model. Tests
arguably deserve a stronger one, since deciding which tests add value — or
could be deleted — needs more careful reasoning than documentation.

### Release options

Releases are currently created as drafts, to be published by hand, and
don't comment on the issues and pull requests they include. A comment such
as "Included in version 1.2.0" on fixed issues would be a useful record,
but needs an additional GitHub App permission.

*Feedback wanted:* drafts or direct publishing? Comments on released
issues?

## Not yet proven in real use

- **Monthly sweeps** of the whole package — the first scheduled run is
  still ahead.
- **Test coverage suggestions at scale**: generating, running and
  proposing tests, and suggestions for deleting existing ones.
- **The first real release** with the version written to `DESCRIPTION` —
  the release chain has so far only run as a dry run.

## Planned

- **Keepalive for scheduled workflows.** GitHub disables scheduled
  workflows after 60 days without repository activity; a shared workflow
  will keep them running without each repository adding its own fix.
- **Caching for R CMD check**, to speed up repeated runs.
- **Real coverage data** for the test suggestions, e.g. how much each
  proposed test adds.
